flags.name: Rod 'Hot Rod' Hundley
flags.issue: Minor tier tension only: a 2x All-Star (1960, 1961) carrying the lowest 'deep' tier. Defensible — career 8.4 ppg over 431 games is a reserve profile and his All-Star nods came in a thin era — but worth noting. All stats verified correct (StatMuse/Basketball-Reference).

flags.name: Fred Brown
flags.issue: Tier 'role' is disputable: 1976 All-Star, finished 5th in NBA scoring in 1975-76 (23.1 ppg), captain of the 1979 champion Sonics, 14.6 career ppg, and No. 32 retired by Seattle. Profile reads as 'starter'/sixth-man star rather than a role player.

flags.name: Artis Gilmore
flags.issue: Record is tagged league:'nba' but includes an ABA team (Kentucky Colonels) and combined ABA+NBA career totals (24,941 pts includes 5 ABA seasons). Also tier 'allstar' arguably undersells him: 1972 ABA MVP, 1975 ABA champion/Playoffs MVP, 11x All-Star, Hall of Fame — superstar-level in the ABA.

flags.name: Pete Maravich
flags.issue: Jersey 7 is legitimate (Jazz/Celtics, retired by the Jazz) but he is at least equally famous as No. 44 (LSU and Atlanta Hawks, retired by the Hawks). Not a factual error, but 44 is arguably his signature number.

flags.name: Tracy McGrady
flags.issue: Tier 'allstar' is disputable: McGrady is a Hall of Famer with 2 scoring titles (2003, 2004), 7 All-Star and 7 All-NBA selections (2x First Team), and a 32.1 ppg peak — many rankings treat peak T-Mac as superstar-tier. Stats themselves verified correct.

flags.name: Reggie Miller
flags.issue: The '50-40-90 season (1993-94)' accolade looked dubious but VERIFIED TRUE (.503/.421/.908 per multiple sources listing him among the nine 50-40-90 club members) — no correction needed, noting it was adversarially checked.

flags.name: Garrett Temple
flags.issue: Teams array lists only 6 franchises but his own accolade says 12, and StatMuse confirms 16 seasons across 12 teams (missing e.g. Rockets, Bucks, Hornets, Bulls, Pelicans). Also listed at SF; he is primarily a shooting guard (StatMuse lists him SG). Career averages 5.8/2.2 verified correct.

flags.name: Robert Williams III
flags.issue: Career fg_pct 0.72 could not be verified to the exact digit (sources cite season marks of .732 and .736; career is roughly .72-.73). Not refuted, but the value may understate slightly. The 'highest career FG% ever' accolade itself is legitimate.

flags.name: Kawhi Leonard
flags.issue: Career line (20.7/6.4/3.1 in 798 g) verified current through 2025-26, but this record will drift fast — he is mid-resurgence (27.9 ppg season, 7th All-Star, 55-pt high) and the tier 'superstar' is honest.

flags.name: Jonquel Jones
flags.issue: Tier dispute: tagged 'allstar' but resume is superstar-grade — 2021 MVP, 2024 champion & Finals MVP, 6x All-Star, 3x rebounding leader (Wikipedia). Also note '2018 Sixth Player of the Year' was named 'Sixth Woman of the Year' in 2018, and her totals (332 g) only reconcile if they include ~26 mid-2026 games on top of the 306 through 2025 — consistent with live data, not an error.

flags.name: Kayla McBride
flags.issue: Tier dispute: tagged 'starter' but she is a 5x All-Star (listed in the record itself) averaging 18.1 ppg in 2026 — fits 'allstar' tier. Her career line (402 g, 5,899 pts, 14.7 ppg) exceeds through-2025 figures (374 g, 5,382 pts, 14.4 ppg) but reconciles exactly with ~27 games of her 18.1-ppg 2026 season, so the stats are not refutable as errors — just verify the database intends live mid-season totals.

flags.name: Sancho Lyttle
flags.issue: All-Star count disputed between sources: record says '1x All-Star'; StatMuse/Basketball-Reference count 1 official All-Star Game, but Wikipedia and WNBA.com describe her as a two-time All-Star (2009, plus the 2010 'Stars at the Sun' selection). Not a clean correction, but the honor is undercounted by some sources' reckoning.

flags.name: Alphonso Ford
flags.issue: Tier 'role' is dubious for a world-league record: he was a EuroLeague star — 2x EuroLeague top scorer (2001, 2002) and the league's annual Top Scorer Trophy is named after him. 'Role' fits his brief NBA stint, not his European career this record describes; allstar tier is more honest.

flags.name: Modestas Paulauskas
flags.issue: Tier 'starter' undersells him: FIBA Hall of Famer (about.fiba.basketball hall-of-famers page), youngest EuroBasket MVP ever (1965, age 20), USSR captain from 1969, 1972 Olympic gold + 1968 bronze, 1967 World champion, 4 EuroBasket golds. Allstar-level resume; also his FIBA Hall of Fame induction is missing from accolades.

flags.name: Juan Antonio San Epifanio (Epi)
flags.issue: Tier 'starter' undersells him: FIBA Hall of Fame (2016), Mister Europa Player of the Year (1984), #15 retired by FC Barcelona, 7 Spanish league titles, widely called one of the greatest European small forwards ever. Accolades also omit FIBA HOF and Mister Europa. Facts as listed are accurate, but tier reads allstar.

flags.name: Oscar Schmidt
flags.issue: Career points figure is disputed across sources: 49,737 (as recorded) is the majority figure (NBA.com, Wikipedia's most-career-points list), but Oscar's own Wikipedia bio states 49,973 over 1,626 games. Not correcting since preponderance of sources supports the record's value, but worth a footnote. Jersey #14 is fine (Brazil/Flamengo, retired at Flamengo), though he also wore 18 (Caserta) and 11 (Pavia).

flags.name: Malloy "The Future" Nesmith
flags.issue: Accolade calls him a 'Harlem legend' but he is a Bronx native (played AT Harlem's Rucker Park). Also, sources confirm he was an original AND1 mixtape signee/featured player, but none confirm he was on the traveling AND1 Mixtape Tour roster — the 'AND1 Mixtape Tour' team entry is unverified.

flags.name: Frank "Shake & Bake" Streety
flags.issue: Tier 'role' may undersell him: sources call him the original king of the shake-and-bake, a Rucker Pro League legend who played against Dr. J, Tiny Archibald and World B. Free, and a Harlem Globetrotters showman. 'allstar' (street tier) is more defensible than 'role'.

flags.name: Earl "The Goat" Manigault
flags.issue: Minor: Goat Park (Happy Warrior Playground) is usually placed at Amsterdam Ave around W 98th–99th St; most sources say '99th Street and Amsterdam' rather than 'West 98th St'. Not a hard error. Tier and all other accolades verified.

flags.name: James "Twiggy" Sanders
flags.issue: Eras list '1970s, 1980s, 1990s' is technically true but marginal — he joined in 1974 and retired in 1991, so the 1990s span only ~1 year ('three decades' claim is borderline).

flags.name: Adam Morrison
flags.issue: Tier 'starter' is disputable: he led the nation in scoring (28.1 ppg, verified), was a consensus first-team All-American and near-POY, and Gonzaga retired his No. 3. In a college-context database this profile matches 'allstar' (same tier as fellow consensus All-Americans in this set), not 'starter'.

flags.name: Don Barksdale
flags.issue: League tag 'fives' is dubious: his listed teams (Baltimore Bullets, Boston Celtics) and stats (262 G, 11.0/8.0/2.1 — verified vs Basketball-Reference) are NBA; his pre-NBA career was UCLA and AAU (Oakland Bittners), not Negro basketball leagues. Record itself is accurate but appears filed under the wrong league category.

flags.name: Lynette Woodard
flags.issue: Possible tier undersell: as the women's major-college all-time scoring leader (3,649 pts, 26.3 ppg — verified), 4x All-American, Olympic gold medalist, and Hall of Famer, she is the women's analogue of Maravich (tagged 'superstar' here); 'allstar' may be a tier too low.
